title: Derive an herdr-legal agent slug from the pane id
action: REWORK after a NEEDS_REVISION verdict on commit c30f6320. The fix itself passed judging: sanitize_agent_slug in packages/bee-rs/crates/fleet/src/backend/herdr.rs survived 19 adversarial inputs plus 200,000 fuzz strings against an independently written legality check, the out-of-scope test literal (w4-pB to w4-pb in packages/bee-rs/crates/fleet/tests/herdr_backend.rs) was the minimum edit and weakened no assertion, and nothing on the do-not-change list moved. Do not touch any of that. THE FAILURE IS COVERAGE, and it is this feature's own recurring shape for the tenth time: the test exercises only ONE clause of the function it pins. Its sole input is the pane id w4:pG, which is already lowercase-safe apart from the case fold and is already short and already starts with a letter — so two of the three clauses are never reached. The judge proved it by mutation: deleting the leading-letter insert, and deleting the 32-character truncate, EACH leave the whole fleet crate green. The function is private to the crate, so no other suite can catch either. THE FIX. Add inputs to the existing test decide_start_derives_an_herdr_legal_slug_from_an_uppercase_pane_id (or a sibling beside it) so every clause of the rule has an input that reaches it: one pane id whose derived slug would not start with a lowercase letter, and one long enough that the derived slug would exceed 32 characters. Keep asserting against the independently written is_legal_herdr_agent_name predicate rather than hardcoded expected strings — that part was judged correct and is the reason the test states a contract at all. Prove it the way the judge did, and say so on the cap: with the test in place, deleting the leading-letter insert must fail a NAMED test, and deleting the truncate must fail a NAMED test. A test added without that red-first check is not evidence. Change no production code — if a clause turns out to be genuinely unreachable rather than merely untested, say so on the cap instead of deleting it.

report.outcome: Every clause of the agent-slug rule now has a test input that reaches it: the case fold (w4:pG), the leading-lowercase-letter repair (9:pA), and the 32-character truncation (a 43-character pane id). The assertion still runs against the independently written is_legal_herdr_agent_name predicate rather than hardcoded expected strings. Only the test body changed; sanitize_agent_slug is untouched and no clause turned out to be unreachable. RED-FIRST: all three mutations were re-applied and each is killed by a NAMED test — removing the leading-letter insert fails the reworked test at herdr.rs:1155 on 9:pA, removing slug.truncate(32) fails it at herdr.rs:1158 on the long pane id, and removing the lowercase fold fails the integration test start_spawns_a_fresh_agent_using_the_constructed_kind_never_a_hardcoded_literal. An independent judge confirmed 3 of 3 killed and the production file byte-identical after restore.
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml — exit 0 under pipefail, 30 green result blocks — workspace scope, because the changed file is a crate the whole workspace links

checks.evidence: Standalone fuzz of an exact copy of sanitize_agent_slug (herdr.rs:614) against an independently written herdr rule check: 19 adversarial fixed inputs (w4:pG, w10:pAF, empty string, '::', '9:pA', '-lead', '_lead', unicode incl. combining mark and emoji, 40-char and 42-char inputs, whitespace-only) plus 200,000 pseudo-random fuzz strings over U+0000..U+02FF and emoji, lengths 0-59 — output: 'done, bad=0'. Every output starts with a lowercase letter, uses only [a-z0-9_-], and is 1-32 chars. truncate(32) cannot panic on a char boundary because every char is ASCII after the mapping step. No failing input found.

checks.failure_signature: mutation-survival: leading-letter fix and truncation clauses of sanitize_agent_slug are untested — deleting either leaves cargo test -p fleet fully green
checks.evidence: The new test (herdr.rs:1133 decide_start_derives_an_herdr_legal_slug_from_an_uppercase_pane_id) does assert the rule via is_legal_herdr_agent_name (herdr.rs:1127, written independently, checks all three clauses) — good. Mutation results: M1 drop-the-lowercasing (uppercase passes charset) -> KILLED, that named test fails with 'got "w4-pG"'. M2 delete the 'if !starts_with_lowercase_letter { slug.insert(0, 'a'); }' block -> SURVIVES: cargo test -p fleet all green (53+11+17+6 passed). M3 delete 'slug.truncate(32);' -> SURVIVES: all green (53+11+17+6 passed). Cause: the test's only input is w4:pG (5 chars, leading lowercase 'w'), so the leading-letter and 32-char clauses of the asserted rule are never exercised. sanitize_agent_slug is private to crates/fleet (rg over the workspace shows no reference outside crates/fleet), so the fleet suite is the complete kill-surface. Mitigation note for the orchestrator: both surviving clauses are defensive — every real herdr pane id is w<N>:p<X>, which always yields a short leading-'w' slug — and the cell's letter asked for 'a test ... for an uppercase pane id', which exists and is rule-shaped. But under this dispatch's stated criterion (a surviving mutation is a FAIL) the check fails; two extra assert lines (e.g. inputs '9:pA' and a 40-char id) close it.
